cloze.title: 四选一完形填空

parts.text: Marie Tharp, who mapped the ocean floor and identified the Mid-Atlantic Ridge rift valley, is also mentioned in A-level geology. She provided

evidence for continental drift, despite being prohibited from boarding research vessels for years and having her ideas dismissed as “girl talk”.

Finally, Rosalind Franklin is included in two biology specifications for her X-ray

work revealing the double-helix structure of DNA. Her essential data was used without attribution during her lifetime.

At GCSE level, when science is compulsory for all students, Franklin is the only woman mentioned. At A-level, Lehmann and Tharp appear

in geology, a subject taken by less than 2% of science students.

For centuries, social, economic, and institutional barriers limited women’s formal participation in science. Despite this, women made numerous key

, and these are already taught to UK 14–18-year-olds. But the names of the women behind them did not make it onto the page.

Why representation matters

Diversity within scientific fields drives creativity and innovation, benefiting all of society. Yet women remain

. They make up only around one third of the global scientific community, with similar figures seen within the UK workforce.

This disparity starts early on in schools: although science uptake is balanced at Key Stage 4, just two years later at Key Stage 5, physics,

and further mathematics only see participation from girls at 24.1%, 37.3% and 26.9% respectively in 2025. This imbalance continues into university, where women make up roughly 25% of physics undergraduate students in the UK.

Introducing relatable female role models into the

directly boosts girls’ confidence and fosters positive attitudes towards scientific careers. But because specifications dictate mandatory exam content, teachers currently have to go out of their way to add female figures on top of busy workloads. By making small,

changes directly to national specifications, we can make inclusion standard practice across all schools.

We propose inserting one female scientist per subject into topics that are already compulsory, but where the woman’s name is

.

This means introducing Marie Skłodowska-Curie, who coined the term radioactivity and discovered polonium and radium, when teaching atomic structure and radioactivity, and Lise Meitner, who provided the first theoretical explanation of nuclear fission, when discussing this concept. GCSE
should include Jocelyn Bell Burnell, who discovered pulsars: rotating neutron stars used as cosmic clocks.

reading.title: 主旨、理解与信息定位
reading.instruction: 阅读原文后回答 5 道选择题：1 道主旨、1 道内容理解、1 道段落细节、2 道信息定位。段落细节题以题干指定段落为准。

questions.prompt: Which statement best summarises the overall focus of this article?
options: Better preparation for teachers is central to supporting pupils with dyslexia.
Regular park visits are associated with measurable differences in children's mental health.
Science curricula often overlook women whose work helped shape scientific knowledge.
A long-term study links public prekindergarten attendance to better later educational outcomes.
questions.explanation: 把标题与全文各段的中心内容连起来判断主旨，避免把同一主题下的其他话题当成本文重点。
questions.evidence: In our new study, led by researchers at the University of Cambridge alongside IncludeHer, a collaborative project working to improve the representation of women in school science education, we analysed over 40 science specifications: the knowledge required to pass exams.

questions.prompt: Why do omissions in early science courses matter?
options: Curriculum content has no effect on perceptions of scientists.
Students never remember anything from school.
Later science learning is completely unrelated to earlier learning.
These courses form foundations that can influence people for life.
questions.explanation: 第 3 段提供了作答依据。正确选项用不同说法表达了文中的信息；请比较范围、数量、因果关系与限定词。
questions.evidence: Because these early stages form the foundation of our science education, their omissions stick with us for life.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is explicitly made in paragraph 8?
options: For physics, they can include Annie Jump Cannon when describing the classification of stars.
Leaving women out of national specifications sends an implicit message about who science is really for.
By making small, targeted changes directly to national specifications, we can make inclusion standard practice across all schools.
Inge Lehmann, who discovered that the Earth has a solid inner core surrounded by a liquid outer core, is cited in A-level Geology via the “Lehmann discontinuity”.
questions.explanation: 定位第 8 段，比较四个选项的具体信息。其余选项来自本文其他段落，并非本段明确陈述的内容。
questions.evidence: Inge Lehmann, who discovered that the Earth has a solid inner core surrounded by a liquid outer core, is cited in A-level Geology via the “Lehmann discontinuity”.
